1	# Scientific material: magnetic-dipole electromagnetic forward modeling
2	
3	This task uses the electromagnetic forward-modeling capabilities of SimPEG.
4	The supplied source snapshot is the historical SimPEG revision identified in
5	`metadata.json`; it includes the electromagnetic source, field, receiver, and
6	finite-volume simulation modules needed for the experiment.
7	
8	## Primary project reference
9	
10	Rowan Cockett, Seogi Kang, Lindsey J. Heagy, Adam Pidlisecky, and Douglas W.
11	Oldenburg, *SimPEG: An open source framework for simulation and gradient based
12	parameter estimation in geophysical applications*, Computers & Geosciences 85
13	(2015), 142-154.
14	
15	- DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2015.09.015>
16	- Project: <https://github.com/simpeg/simpeg>
17	- License of the source snapshot: MIT; see `source/LICENSE`.
18	
19	## Electromagnetic method reference
20	
21	Lindsey J. Heagy, Rowan Cockett, Seogi Kang, Gudni K. Rosenkjaer, and Douglas
22	W. Oldenburg, *A framework for simulation and inversion in electromagnetics*,
23	Computers & Geosciences 107 (2017), 1-19.
24	
25	- DOI: <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cageo.2017.06.018>
26	- The matching citation is also included in `source/CITATION.rst`.
27	
28	This paper describes the electromagnetic formulation used by SimPEG: Maxwell's
29	equations are discretized on a finite-volume mesh, with different field
30	quantities associated with different mesh entities. The package supports
31	frequency-domain and time-domain forward problems and exposes multiple
32	representations of the electromagnetic fields. A physical source should not
33	change its meaning merely because an equivalent supported representation is
34	selected.
35	
36	## Continuous-space reference model
37	
38	For a magnetic dipole with moment vector \(\mathbf m = m\hat{\mathbf u}\),
39	located at \(\mathbf r_0\), define \(\mathbf R=\mathbf r-\mathbf r_0\),
40	\(R=\lVert\mathbf R\rVert\), and \(\hat{\mathbf R}=\mathbf R/R\). In a
41	homogeneous unbounded medium the magnetostatic magnetic flux density is
42	
43	\[
44	 \mathbf B(\mathbf r) =
45	 \frac{\mu}{4\pi R^3}
46	 \left(3(\mathbf m\cdot\hat{\mathbf R})\hat{\mathbf R}-\mathbf m\right),
47	 \qquad \mathbf H=\mathbf B/\mu.
48	\]
49	
50	The field is linear in dipole moment, rotates with the dipole orientation, and
51	changes with the medium permeability. Components that are analytically zero
52	should not be used as a relative-error denominator. At the experiment level,
53	observations expressed as magnetic field and magnetic flux density should
54	remain compatible after applying the constitutive relation for the same
55	medium.
56	
57	## Discrete representation and interpretation
58	
59	The finite-volume implementation represents vector quantities on mesh entities
60	appropriate to their role in the discrete Maxwell equations. A curl is a
61	linear map between those entity spaces, while mass or inner-product matrices
62	perform the corresponding integral pairing. The field representation and the
63	source discretization must describe the same physical vector field after these
64	operations.
65	
66	The API documentation and equations in the supplied source snapshot are the
67	main offline reference for the representation conventions. Read the
68	electromagnetics simulation, source, field, and receiver modules as a connected
69	workflow. Their equations and docstrings explain which discrete spaces are
70	used by supported formulations and how source terms enter the forward problem.
71	They do not identify the defect or prescribe a repair. Use the public
72	reproduction and the independent continuous-space relation above to determine
73	whether the implementation preserves the physical source semantics.
74	
75	## Reproducibility material
76	
77	The official project and method references are available at the URLs above.

3	import numpy as np
4	from discretize import TensorMesh
5	from scipy.constants import mu_0
6	
7	from simpeg import maps
8	import simpeg.electromagnetics.frequency_domain as fdem
9	
10	
11	def _mesh(case: dict) -> TensorMesh:
12	    cell = float(case["cell_size_m"])
13	    core = int(case["n_core"])
14	    padding = int(case["n_padding"])
15	    widths = [(cell, padding, -1.3), (cell, core), (cell, padding, 1.3)]
16	    return TensorMesh([widths, widths, widths], origin="CCC")
17	
18	
19	def _predict(
20	    case: dict,
21	    *,
22	    mesh: TensorMesh,
23	) -> np.ndarray:
24	    model = np.full(mesh.n_cells, float(case["conductivity_s_per_m"]))
25	    locations = np.asarray(case["receiver_locations_m"], dtype=float)
26	    receiver = fdem.receivers.PointMagneticField(
27	        locations, orientation=case["receiver_orientation"], component="real"
28	    )
29	    source = fdem.sources.MagDipole(
30	        [receiver],
31	        location=np.zeros(3),
32	        frequency=float(case["frequency_hz"]),
33	        moment=float(case["dipole_moment"]),
34	        orientation=case["dipole_orientation"],
35	        mu=float(case["relative_permeability"]) * mu_0,
36	    )
37	    simulation = fdem.simulation.Simulation3DMagneticField(
38	        mesh,
39	        survey=fdem.Survey([source]),
40	        sigmaMap=maps.IdentityMap(),
41	    )
42	    return np.asarray(simulation.dpred(model), dtype=float).reshape(-1)
43	
44	
45	def run_public_case(case: dict) -> dict[str, object]:
46	    mesh = _mesh(case)
47	    predicted = _predict(case, mesh=mesh)
48	    finite = bool(predicted.size > 0 and np.all(np.isfinite(predicted)))
49	    return {
50	        "finite": finite,
51	        "receiver_count": int(predicted.size),
52	        "observation_norm": float(np.linalg.norm(predicted)) if finite else None,
53	        "observation_span": float(np.ptp(predicted)) if finite else None,
54	        "nonzero_observation_count": (
55	            int(np.count_nonzero(np.abs(predicted) > np.finfo(float).eps))
56	            if finite
57	            else 0
58	        ),
59	    }

21	class BaseFDEMSimulation(BaseEMSimulation):
22	    r"""Base finite volume FDEM simulation class.
23	
24	    This class is used to define properties and methods necessary for solving
25	    3D frequency-domain EM problems. For a :math:`+i\omega t` Fourier convention,
26	    Maxwell's equations are expressed as:
27	
28	    .. math::
29	        \begin{align}
30	        \nabla \times \vec{E} + i\omega \vec{B} &= - i \omega \vec{S}_m \\
31	        \nabla \times \vec{H} - \vec{J} &= \vec{S}_e
32	        \end{align}
33	
34	    where the constitutive relations between fields and fluxes are given by:
35	
36	    * :math:`\vec{J} = \sigma \vec{E}`
37	    * :math:`\vec{B} = \mu \vec{H}`
38	
39	    and:
40	
41	    * :math:`\vec{S}_m` represents a magnetic source term
42	    * :math:`\vec{S}_e` represents a current source term
43	
44	    Child classes of ``BaseFDEMSimulation`` solve the above expression numerically
45	    for various cases using mimetic finite volume.
46	
47	    Parameters
48	    ----------
49	    mesh : discretize.base.BaseMesh
50	        The mesh.
51	    survey : .frequency_domain.survey.Survey
52	        The frequency-domain EM survey.
53	    forward_only : bool, optional
54	        If ``True``, the factorization for the inverse of the system matrix at each
55	        frequency is discarded after the fields are computed at that frequency.
56	        If ``False``, the factorizations of the system matrices for all frequencies are stored.
57	    permittivity : (n_cells,) numpy.ndarray, optional
58	        Dielectric permittivity (F/m) defined on the entire mesh. If ``None``, electric displacement
59	        is ignored. Please note that `permittivity` is not an invertible property, and that future
60	        development will result in the deprecation of this propery.
61	    storeJ : bool, optional
62	        Whether to compute and store the sensitivity matrix.
63	    """
64	
65	    fieldsPair = FieldsFDEM
66	    permittivity = props.PhysicalProperty("Dielectric permittivity (F/m)")
67	
68	    def __init__(
69	        self,
70	        mesh,
71	        survey=None,
72	        forward_only=False,
73	        permittivity=None,
74	        storeJ=False,
75	        **kwargs,
76	    ):
77	        super().__init__(mesh=mesh, survey=survey, **kwargs)
78	        self.forward_only = forward_only
79	        if permittivity is not None:
80	            warnings.warn(
81	                "Simulations using permittivity have not yet been thoroughly tested and derivatives are not implemented. Contributions welcome!",
82	                stacklevel=2,
83	            )
84	        self.permittivity = permittivity
85	        self.storeJ = storeJ
86	
87	    @property
88	    def survey(self):
89	        """The FDEM survey object.
90	
91	        Returns
92	        -------
93	        .frequency_domain.survey.Survey
94	            The FDEM survey object.
95	        """
96	        if self._survey is None:
97	            raise AttributeError("Simulation must have a survey set")
98	        return self._survey
99	
100	    @survey.setter
101	    def survey(self, value):
102	        if value is not None:
103	            value = validate_type("survey", value, Survey, cast=False)
104	        self._survey = value
105	        self._survey = value
106	
107	    @property
108	    def storeJ(self):
109	        """Whether to compute and store the sensitivity matrix.
110	
111	        Returns
112	        -------
113	        bool
114	            Whether to compute and store the sensitivity matrix.
115	        """
116	        return self._storeJ
117	
118	    @storeJ.setter
119	    def storeJ(self, value):
120	        self._storeJ = validate_type("storeJ", value, bool)
121	
122	    @property
123	    def forward_only(self):
124	        """Whether to store the factorizations of the inverses of the system matrices.
125	
126	        If ``True``, the factorization for the inverse of the system matrix at each
127	        frequency is discarded after the fields are computed at that frequency.
128	        If ``False``, the factorizations of the system matrices for all frequencies are stored.
129	
130	        Returns
131	        -------
132	        bool
133	            Whether to store the factorizations of the inverses of the system matrices.
134	        """
135	        return self._forward_only
136	
137	    @forward_only.setter
138	    def forward_only(self, value):
139	        self._forward_only = validate_type("forward_only", value, bool)
140	
141	    def _get_admittivity(self, freq):
142	        if self.permittivity is not None:
143	            return self.sigma + 1j * self.permittivity * omega(freq)
144	        else:
145	            return self.sigma
146	
147	    def _get_face_admittivity_property_matrix(
148	        self, freq, invert_model=False, invert_matrix=False
149	    ):
150	        """
151	        Face inner product matrix with permittivity and resistivity
152	        """
153	        yhat = self._get_admittivity(freq)
154	        return self.mesh.get_face_inner_product(
155	            yhat, invert_model=invert_model, invert_matrix=invert_matrix
156	        )
157	
158	    def _get_edge_admittivity_property_matrix(
159	        self, freq, invert_model=False, invert_matrix=False
160	    ):
161	        """
162	        Face inner product matrix with permittivity and resistivity
163	        """
164	        yhat = self._get_admittivity(freq)
165	        return self.mesh.get_edge_inner_product(
166	            yhat, invert_model=invert_model, invert_matrix=invert_matrix
167	        )
168	
169	    # @profile
170	    def fields(self, m=None):
171	        """Compute and return the fields for the model provided.
172	
173	        Parameters
174	        ----------
175	        m : (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
176	            The model.
177	
178	        Returns
179	        -------
180	        .frequency_domain.fields.FieldsFDEM
181	            The FDEM fields object.
182	        """
183	
184	        if m is not None:
185	            self.model = m
186	
187	        try:
188	            self.Ainv
189	        except AttributeError:
190	            self.Ainv = len(self.survey.frequencies) * [None]
191	
192	        f = self.fieldsPair(self)
193	
194	        for i_f, freq in enumerate(self.survey.frequencies):
195	            A = self.getA(freq)
196	            rhs = self.getRHS(freq)
197	            Ainv = self.solver(A, **self.solver_opts)
198	            u = Ainv * rhs
199	            if not self.forward_only:
200	                self.Ainv[i_f] = Ainv
201	
202	            Srcs = self.survey.get_sources_by_frequency(freq)
203	            f[Srcs, self._solutionType] = u
204	        return f
205	
206	    # @profile
207	    def Jvec(self, m, v, f=None):
208	        r"""Compute the sensitivity matrix times a vector.
209	
210	        Where :math:`\mathbf{d}` are the data, :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the model parameters,
211	        and the sensitivity matrix is defined as:
212	
213	        .. math::
214	            \mathbf{J} = \dfrac{\partial \mathbf{d}}{\partial \mathbf{m}}
215	
216	        this method computes and returns the matrix-vector product:
217	
218	        .. math::
219	            \mathbf{J v}
220	
221	        for a given vector :math:`v`.
222	
223	        Parameters
224	        ----------
225	        m : (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
226	            The model parameters.
227	        v : (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
228	            The vector.
229	        f : .frequency_domain.fields.FieldsFDEM, optional
230	            Fields solved for all sources.
231	
232	        Returns
233	        -------
234	        (n_data,) numpy.ndarray
235	            The sensitivity matrix times a vector.
236	        """
237	
238	        if f is None:
239	            f = self.fields(m)
240	
241	        self.model = m
242	
243	        survey_slices = self.survey.get_all_slices()
244	        Jv = np.full(self.survey.nD, fill_value=np.nan)
245	
246	        for nf, freq in enumerate(self.survey.frequencies):
247	            for src in self.survey.get_sources_by_frequency(freq):
248	                u_src = f[src, self._solutionType]
249	                dA_dm_v = self.getADeriv(freq, u_src, v, adjoint=False)
250	                dRHS_dm_v = self.getRHSDeriv(freq, src, v)
251	                du_dm_v = self.Ainv[nf] * (-dA_dm_v + dRHS_dm_v)
252	                for rx in src.receiver_list:
253	                    src_rx_slice = survey_slices[src, rx]
254	                    Jv[src_rx_slice] = mkvc(
255	                        rx.evalDeriv(src, self.mesh, f, du_dm_v=du_dm_v, v=v)
256	                    )
257	
258	        return Jv
259	
260	    def Jtvec(self, m, v, f=None):
261	        r"""Compute the adjoint sensitivity matrix times a vector.
262	
263	        Where :math:`\mathbf{d}` are the data, :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the model parameters,
264	        and the sensitivity matrix is defined as:
265	
266	        .. math::
267	            \mathbf{J} = \dfrac{\partial \mathbf{d}}{\partial \mathbf{m}}
268	
269	        this method computes and returns the matrix-vector product:
270	
271	        .. math::
272	            \mathbf{J^T v}
273	
274	        for a given vector :math:`v`.
275	
276	        Parameters
277	        ----------
278	        m : (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
279	            The model parameters.
280	        v : (n_data,) numpy.ndarray
281	            The vector.
282	        f : .frequency_domain.fields.FieldsFDEM, optional
283	            Fields solved for all sources.
284	
285	        Returns
286	        -------
287	        (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
288	            The adjoint sensitivity matrix times a vector.
289	        """
290	
291	        if f is None:
292	            f = self.fields(m)
293	
294	        self.model = m
295	
296	        # Get dict of flat array slices for each source-receiver pair in the survey
297	        survey_slices = self.survey.get_all_slices()
298	
299	        Jtv = np.zeros(m.size)
300	
301	        for nf, freq in enumerate(self.survey.frequencies):
302	            for src in self.survey.get_sources_by_frequency(freq):
303	                u_src = f[src, self._solutionType]
304	                df_duT_sum = 0
305	                df_dmT_sum = 0
306	                for rx in src.receiver_list:
307	                    src_rx_slice = survey_slices[src, rx]
308	                    df_duT, df_dmT = rx.evalDeriv(
309	                        src, self.mesh, f, v=v[src_rx_slice], adjoint=True
310	                    )
311	                    if not isinstance(df_duT, Zero):
312	                        df_duT_sum += df_duT
313	                    if not isinstance(df_dmT, Zero):
314	                        df_dmT_sum += df_dmT
315	
316	                ATinvdf_duT = self.Ainv[nf] * df_duT_sum
317	
318	                dA_dmT = self.getADeriv(freq, u_src, ATinvdf_duT, adjoint=True)
319	                dRHS_dmT = self.getRHSDeriv(freq, src, ATinvdf_duT, adjoint=True)
320	                du_dmT = -dA_dmT + dRHS_dmT
321	
322	                df_dmT_sum += du_dmT
323	                Jtv += np.real(df_dmT_sum)
324	
325	        return mkvc(Jtv)
326	
327	    def getJ(self, m, f=None):
328	        r"""Generate the full sensitivity matrix.
329	
330	        This method generates and stores the full sensitivity matrix for the
331	        model provided. I.e.:
332	
333	        .. math::
334	            \mathbf{J} = \dfrac{\partial \mathbf{d}}{\partial \mathbf{m}}
335	
336	        where :math:`\mathbf{d}` are the data and :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the model parameters.
337	
338	        Parameters
339	        ----------
340	        m : (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
341	            The model parameters.
342	        f : .static.resistivity.fields.FieldsDC, optional
343	            Fields solved for all sources.
344	
345	        Returns
346	        -------
347	        (n_data, n_param) numpy.ndarray
348	            The full sensitivity matrix.
349	        """
350	        self.model = m
351	
352	        if getattr(self, "_Jmatrix", None) is None:
353	            if f is None:
354	                f = self.fields(m)
355	
356	            Ainv = self.Ainv
357	            m_size = self.model.size
358	
359	            Jmatrix = np.zeros((self.survey.nD, m_size))
360	
361	            # Get dict of flat array slices for each source-receiver pair in the survey
362	            survey_slices = self.survey.get_all_slices()
363	
364	            for A_i, freq in zip(Ainv, self.survey.frequencies):
365	                for src in self.survey.get_sources_by_frequency(freq):
366	                    u_src = f[src, self._solutionType]
367	
368	                    for rx in src.receiver_list:
369	                        v = np.eye(rx.nD, dtype=float)
370	
371	                        df_duT, df_dmT = rx.evalDeriv(
372	                            src, self.mesh, f, v=v, adjoint=True
373	                        )
374	
375	                        df_duT = np.hstack([df_duT])
376	                        ATinvdf_duT = A_i * df_duT
377	                        dA_dmT = self.getADeriv(freq, u_src, ATinvdf_duT, adjoint=True)
378	                        dRHS_dmT = self.getRHSDeriv(
379	                            freq, src, ATinvdf_duT, adjoint=True
380	                        )
381	                        du_dmT = -dA_dmT
382	
383	                        if not isinstance(dRHS_dmT, Zero):
384	                            du_dmT += dRHS_dmT
385	                        if not isinstance(df_dmT[0], Zero):
386	                            du_dmT += np.hstack(df_dmT)
387	
388	                        block = np.array(du_dmT, dtype=complex).real.T
389	
390	                        src_rx_slice = survey_slices[src, rx]
391	                        Jmatrix[src_rx_slice] = block
392	
393	            self._Jmatrix = Jmatrix
394	
395	        return self._Jmatrix
396	
397	    def getJtJdiag(self, m, W=None, f=None):
398	        r"""Return the diagonal of :math:`\mathbf{J^T J}`.
399	
400	        Where :math:`\mathbf{d}` are the data and :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the model parameters,
401	        the sensitivity matrix :math:`\mathbf{J}` is defined as:
402	
403	        .. math::
404	            \mathbf{J} = \dfrac{\partial \mathbf{d}}{\partial \mathbf{m}}
405	
406	        This method returns the diagonals of :math:`\mathbf{J^T J}`. When the
407	        *W* input argument is used to include a diagonal weighting matrix
408	        :math:`\mathbf{W}`, this method returns the diagonal of
409	        :math:`\mathbf{W^T J^T J W}`.
410	
411	        Parameters
412	        ----------
413	        m : (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
414	            The model parameters.
415	        W : (n_param, n_param) scipy.sparse.csr_matrix
416	            A diagonal weighting matrix.
417	        f : .frequency_domain.fields.FieldsFDEM, optional
418	            Fields solved for all sources.
419	
420	        Returns
421	        -------
422	        (n_param,) numpy.ndarray
423	            The diagonals.
424	        """
425	        self.model = m
426	
427	        if getattr(self, "_gtgdiag", None) is None:
428	            J = self.getJ(m, f=f)
429	
430	            if W is None:
431	                W = np.ones(J.shape[0])
432	            else:
433	                W = W.diagonal() ** 2
434	
435	            diag = np.einsum("i,ij,ij->j", W, J, J)
436	
437	            self._gtgdiag = diag
438	
439	        return self._gtgdiag
440	
441	    # @profile
442	    def getSourceTerm(self, freq):
443	        r"""Returns the discrete source terms for the frequency provided.
444	
445	        This method computes and returns the discrete magnetic and electric source
446	        terms for all soundings at the frequency provided. The exact shape and
447	        implementation of the source terms when solving for the fields at each frequency
448	        is formulation dependent.
449	
450	        For definitions of the discrete magnetic (:math:`\mathbf{s_m}`) and electric
451	        (:math:`\mathbf{s_e}`) source terms for each simulation, see the *Notes* sections
452	        of the docstrings for:
453	
454	        * :class:`.frequency_domain.Simulation3DElectricField`
455	        * :class:`.frequency_domain.Simulation3DMagneticField`
456	        * :class:`.frequency_domain.Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
457	        * :class:`.frequency_domain.Simulation3DMagneticFluxDensity`
458	
459	        Parameters
460	        ----------
461	        freq : float
462	            The frequency in Hz.
463	
464	        Returns
465	        -------
466	        s_m : numpy.ndarray
467	            The magnetic sources terms. (n_faces, n_sources) for EB-formulations. (n_edges, n_sources) for HJ-formulations.
468	        s_e : numpy.ndarray
469	            The electric sources terms. (n_edges, n_sources) for EB-formulations. (n_faces, n_sources) for HJ-formulations.
470	        """
471	        Srcs = self.survey.get_sources_by_frequency(freq)
472	        n_fields = sum(src._fields_per_source for src in Srcs)
473	        if self._formulation == "EB":
474	            s_m = np.zeros((self.mesh.nF, n_fields), dtype=complex, order="F")
475	            s_e = np.zeros((self.mesh.nE, n_fields), dtype=complex, order="F")
476	        elif self._formulation == "HJ":
477	            s_m = np.zeros((self.mesh.nE, n_fields), dtype=complex, order="F")
478	            s_e = np.zeros((self.mesh.nF, n_fields), dtype=complex, order="F")
479	
480	        i = 0
481	        for src in Srcs:
482	            ii = i + src._fields_per_source
483	            smi, sei = src.eval(self)
484	            if not isinstance(smi, Zero) and smi.ndim == 1:
485	                smi = smi[:, None]
486	            if not isinstance(sei, Zero) and sei.ndim == 1:
487	                sei = sei[:, None]
488	            s_m[:, i:ii] = s_m[:, i:ii] + smi
489	            s_e[:, i:ii] = s_e[:, i:ii] + sei
490	            i = ii
491	        return s_m, s_e
492	
493	    @property
494	    def _delete_on_model_update(self):
495	        """List of model-dependent attributes to clean upon model update.
496	
497	        Some of the FDEM simulation's attributes are model-dependent. This property specifies
498	        the model-dependent attributes that much be cleared when the model is updated.
499	
500	        Returns
501	        -------
502	        list of str
503	            List of the model-dependent attributes to clean upon model update.
504	        """
505	        toDelete = super()._delete_on_model_update
506	        return toDelete + ["_Jmatrix", "_gtgdiag"]

513	
514	class Simulation3DElectricField(BaseFDEMSimulation):
515	    r"""3D FDEM simulation in terms of the electric field.
516	
517	    This simulation solves for the electric field at each frequency.
518	    In this formulation, the electric fields are defined on mesh edges and the
519	    magnetic flux density is defined on mesh faces; i.e. it is an EB formulation.
520	    See the *Notes* section for a comprehensive description of the formulation.
521	
522	    Parameters
523	    ----------
524	    mesh : discretize.base.BaseMesh
525	        The mesh.
526	    survey : .frequency_domain.survey.Survey
527	        The frequency-domain EM survey.
528	    forward_only : bool, optional
529	        If ``True``, the factorization for the inverse of the system matrix at each
530	        frequency is discarded after the fields are computed at that frequency.
531	        If ``False``, the factorizations of the system matrices for all frequencies are stored.
532	    permittivity : (n_cells,) numpy.ndarray, optional
533	        Dielectric permittivity (F/m) defined on the entire mesh. If ``None``, electric displacement
534	        is ignored. Please note that `permittivity` is not an invertible property, and that future
535	        development will result in the deprecation of this propery.
536	    storeJ : bool, optional
537	        Whether to compute and store the sensitivity matrix.
538	
539	    Notes
540	    -----
541	    Here, we start with the Maxwell's equations in the frequency-domain where a
542	    :math:`+i\omega t` Fourier convention is used:
543	
544	    .. math::
545	        \begin{align}
546	        &\nabla \times \vec{E} + i\omega \vec{B} = - i \omega \vec{S}_m \\
547	        &\nabla \times \vec{H} - \vec{J} = \vec{S}_e
548	        \end{align}
549	
550	    where :math:`\vec{S}_e` is an electric source term that defines a source current density,
551	    and :math:`\vec{S}_m` magnetic source term that defines a source magnetic flux density.
552	    We define the constitutive relations for the electrical conductivity :math:`\sigma`
553	    and magnetic permeability :math:`\mu` as:
554	
555	    .. math::
556	        \vec{J} &= \sigma \vec{E} \\
557	        \vec{H} &= \mu^{-1} \vec{B}
558	
559	    We then take the inner products of all previous expressions with a vector test function :math:`\vec{u}`.
560	    Through vector calculus identities and the divergence theorem, we obtain:
561	
562	    .. math::
563	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot (\nabla \times \vec{E}) \, dv
564	        + i \omega \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{B} \, dv
565	        = - i \omega \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{S}_m \, dv \\
566	        & \int_\Omega (\nabla \times \vec{u}) \cdot \vec{H} \, dv
567	        - \oint_{\partial \Omega} \vec{u} \cdot (\vec{H} \times \hat{n}) \, da
568	        - \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{J} \, dv
569	        = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{S}_j \, dv \\
570	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{J} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \sigma \vec{E} \, dv \\
571	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{H} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \mu^{-1} \vec{B} \, dv
572	
573	    Assuming natural boundary conditions, the surface integral is zero.
574	
575	    The above expressions are discretized in space according to the finite volume method.
576	    The discrete electric fields :math:`\mathbf{e}` are defined on mesh edges,
577	    and the discrete magnetic flux densities :math:`\mathbf{b}` are defined on mesh faces.
578	    This implies :math:`\mathbf{j}` must be defined on mesh edges and :math:`\mathbf{h}` must
579	    be defined on mesh faces. Where :math:`\mathbf{u_e}` and :math:`\mathbf{u_f}` represent
580	    test functions discretized to edges and faces, respectively, we obtain the following
581	    set of discrete inner-products:
582	
583	    .. math::
584	        &\mathbf{u_f^T M_f C e} + i \omega \mathbf{u_f^T M_f b} = - i \omega \mathbf{u_f^T M_f s_m} \\
585	        &\mathbf{u_e^T C^T M_f h} - \mathbf{u_e^T M_e j} = \mathbf{u_e^T s_e} \\
586	        &\mathbf{u_e^T M_e j} = \mathbf{u_e^T M_{e \sigma} e} \\
587	        &\mathbf{u_f^T M_f h} = \mathbf{u_f^T M_{f \mu} b}
588	
589	    where
590	
591	    * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the discrete curl operator
592	    * :math:`\mathbf{s_m}` and :math:`\mathbf{s_e}` are the integrated magnetic and electric source terms, respectively
593	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_e}` is the edge inner-product matrix
594	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_f}` is the face inner-product matrix
595	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
596	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
597	
598	    By cancelling like-terms and combining the discrete expressions to solve for the electric field, we obtain:
599	
600	    .. math::
601	        \mathbf{A \, e} = \mathbf{q}
602	
603	    where
604	
605	    * :math:`\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}`
606	    * :math:`\mathbf{q} = - i \omega \mathbf{s_e} - i \omega \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} s_m }`
607	
608	    """
609	
610	    _solutionType = "eSolution"
611	    _formulation = "EB"
612	    fieldsPair = Fields3DElectricField
613	
614	    def getA(self, freq):
615	        r"""System matrix for the frequency provided.
616	
617	        This method returns the system matrix for the frequency provided:
618	
619	        .. math::
620	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}
621	
622	        where
623	
624	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
625	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
626	
627	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DElectricField`
628	        for a full description of the formulation.
629	
630	        Parameters
631	        ----------
632	        freq : float
633	            The frequency in Hz.
634	
635	        Returns
636	        -------
637	        (n_edges, n_edges) sp.sparse.csr_matrix
638	            The system matrix.
639	        """
640	
641	        MfMui = self.MfMui
642	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
643	
644	        if self.permittivity is None:
645	            MeSigma = self.MeSigma
646	            A = C.T.tocsr() * MfMui * C + 1j * omega(freq) * MeSigma
647	        else:
648	            Meyhat = self._get_edge_admittivity_property_matrix(freq)
649	            A = C.T.tocsr() * MfMui * C + 1j * omega(freq) * Meyhat
650	
651	        return A
652	
653	    def getADeriv_sigma(self, freq, u, v, adjoint=False):
654	        r"""Conductivity derivative operation for the system matrix times a vector.
655	
656	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
657	
658	        .. math::
659	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}
660	
661	        where
662	
663	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
664	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
665	
666	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DElectricField`
667	        for a full description of the formulation.
668	
669	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\sigma}` are the set of model parameters defining the conductivity,
670	        :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector and :math:`\mathbf{e}` is the discrete electric field solution, this method assumes
671	        the discrete solution is fixed and returns
672	
673	        .. math::
674	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, e})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\sigma}} \, \mathbf{v}
675	
676	        Or the adjoint operation
677	
678	        .. math::
679	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, e})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\sigma}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
680	
681	        Parameters
682	        ----------
683	        freq : float
684	            The frequency in Hz.
685	        u : (n_edges,) numpy.ndarray
686	            The solution for the fields for the current model at the specified frequency.
687	        v : numpy.ndarray
688	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_edges,) for the adjoint operation.
689	        adjoint : bool
690	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
691	
692	        Returns
693	        -------
694	        numpy.ndarray
695	            Derivative of system matrix times a vector. (n_edges,) for the standard operation.
696	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
697	        """
698	
699	        dMe_dsig_v = self.MeSigmaDeriv(u, v, adjoint)
700	        return 1j * omega(freq) * dMe_dsig_v
701	
702	    def getADeriv_mui(self, freq, u, v, adjoint=False):
703	        r"""Inverse permeability derivative operation for the system matrix times a vector.
704	
705	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
706	
707	        .. math::
708	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}
709	
710	        where
711	
712	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
713	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
714	
715	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DElectricField`
716	        for a full description of the formulation.
717	
718	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\mu}` are the set of model parameters defining the permeability,
719	        :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector and :math:`\mathbf{e}` is the discrete electric field solution, this method assumes
720	        the discrete solution is fixed and returns
721	
722	        .. math::
723	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, e})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\mu}} \, \mathbf{v}
724	
725	        Or the adjoint operation
726	
727	        .. math::
728	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, e})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\mu}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
729	
730	        Parameters
731	        ----------
732	        freq : float
733	            The frequency in Hz.
734	        u : (n_edges,) numpy.ndarray
735	            The solution for the fields for the current model at the specified frequency.
736	        v : numpy.ndarray
737	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_edges,) for the adjoint operation.
738	        adjoint : bool
739	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
740	
741	        Returns
742	        -------
743	        numpy.ndarray
744	            Derivative of system matrix times a vector. (n_edges,) for the standard operation.
745	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
746	        """
747	
748	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
749	
750	        if adjoint:
751	            return self.MfMuiDeriv(C * u).T * (C * v)
752	
753	        return C.T * (self.MfMuiDeriv(C * u) * v)
754	
755	    def getADeriv(self, freq, u, v, adjoint=False):
756	        r"""Derivative operation for the system matrix times a vector.
757	
758	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
759	
760	        .. math::
761	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}
762	
763	        where
764	
765	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
766	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
767	
768	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DElectricField`
769	        for a full description of the formulation.
770	
771	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the set of model parameters defining the electromagnetic properties
772	        :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector and :math:`\mathbf{e}` is the discrete electric field solution, this method assumes
773	        the discrete solution is fixed and returns
774	
775	        .. math::
776	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, e})}{\partial \mathbf{m}} \, \mathbf{v}
777	
778	        Or the adjoint operation
779	
780	        .. math::
781	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, e})}{\partial \mathbf{m}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
782	
783	        Parameters
784	        ----------
785	        freq : float
786	            The frequency in Hz.
787	        u : (n_edges,) numpy.ndarray
788	            The solution for the fields for the current model at the specified frequency.
789	        v : numpy.ndarray
790	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_edges,) for the adjoint operation.
791	        adjoint : bool
792	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
793	
794	        Returns
795	        -------
796	        numpy.ndarray
797	            Derivative of system matrix times a vector. (n_edges,) for the standard operation.
798	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
799	        """
800	        return (
801	            self.getADeriv_sigma(freq, u, v, adjoint)
802	            + self.getADeriv_mui(freq, u, v, adjoint)
803	            # + self.getADeriv_permittivity(freq, u, v, adjoint)
804	        )
805	
806	    def getRHS(self, freq):
807	        r"""Right-hand sides for the given frequency.
808	
809	        This method returns the right-hand sides for the frequency provided.
810	        The right-hand side for each source is constructed according to:
811	
812	        .. math::
813	            \mathbf{q} = - i \omega \mathbf{s_e} - i \omega \mathbf{C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}} s_m }
814

904	class Simulation3DMagneticFluxDensity(BaseFDEMSimulation):
905	    r"""3D FDEM simulation in terms of the magnetic flux field.
906	
907	    This simulation solves for the magnetic flux density at each frequency.
908	    In this formulation, the electric fields are defined on mesh edges and the
909	    magnetic flux density is defined on mesh faces; i.e. it is an EB formulation.
910	    See the *Notes* section for a comprehensive description of the formulation.
911	
912	    Parameters
913	    ----------
914	    mesh : discretize.base.BaseMesh
915	        The mesh.
916	    survey : .frequency_domain.survey.Survey
917	        The frequency-domain EM survey.
918	    forward_only : bool, optional
919	        If ``True``, the factorization for the inverse of the system matrix at each
920	        frequency is discarded after the fields are computed at that frequency.
921	        If ``False``, the factorizations of the system matrices for all frequencies are stored.
922	    permittivity : (n_cells,) numpy.ndarray, optional
923	        Dielectric permittivity (F/m) defined on the entire mesh. If ``None``, electric displacement
924	        is ignored. Please note that `permittivity` is not an invertible property, and that future
925	        development will result in the deprecation of this propery.
926	    storeJ : bool, optional
927	        Whether to compute and store the sensitivity matrix.
928	
929	    Notes
930	    -----
931	    Here, we start with the Maxwell's equations in the frequency-domain where a
932	    :math:`+i\omega t` Fourier convention is used:
933	
934	    .. math::
935	        \begin{align}
936	        &\nabla \times \vec{E} + i\omega \vec{B} = - i \omega \vec{S}_m \\
937	        &\nabla \times \vec{H} - \vec{J} = \vec{S}_e
938	        \end{align}
939	
940	    where :math:`\vec{S}_e` is an electric source term that defines a source current density,
941	    and :math:`\vec{S}_m` magnetic source term that defines a source magnetic flux density.
942	    We define the constitutive relations for the electrical conductivity :math:`\sigma`
943	    and magnetic permeability :math:`\mu` as:
944	
945	    .. math::
946	        \vec{J} &= \sigma \vec{E} \\
947	        \vec{H} &= \mu^{-1} \vec{B}
948	
949	    We then take the inner products of all previous expressions with a vector test function :math:`\vec{u}`.
950	    Through vector calculus identities and the divergence theorem, we obtain:
951	
952	    .. math::
953	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot (\nabla \times \vec{E}) \, dv
954	        + i \omega \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{B} \, dv
955	        = - i \omega \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{S}_m \, dv \\
956	        & \int_\Omega (\nabla \times \vec{u}) \cdot \vec{H} \, dv
957	        - \oint_{\partial \Omega} \vec{u} \cdot (\vec{H} \times \hat{n}) \, da
958	        - \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{J} \, dv
959	        = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{S}_j \, dv \\
960	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{J} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \sigma \vec{E} \, dv \\
961	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{H} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \mu^{-1} \vec{B} \, dv
962	
963	    Assuming natural boundary conditions, the surface integral is zero.
964	
965	    The above expressions are discretized in space according to the finite volume method.
966	    The discrete electric fields :math:`\mathbf{e}` are defined on mesh edges,
967	    and the discrete magnetic flux densities :math:`\mathbf{b}` are defined on mesh faces.
968	    This implies :math:`\mathbf{j}` must be defined on mesh edges and :math:`\mathbf{h}` must
969	    be defined on mesh faces. Where :math:`\mathbf{u_e}` and :math:`\mathbf{u_f}` represent
970	    test functions discretized to edges and faces, respectively, we obtain the following
971	    set of discrete inner-products:
972	
973	    .. math::
974	        &\mathbf{u_f^T M_f C e} + i \omega \mathbf{u_f^T M_f b} = - i \omega \mathbf{u_f^T M_f s_m} \\
975	        &\mathbf{u_e^T C^T M_f h} - \mathbf{u_e^T M_e j} = \mathbf{u_e^T s_e} \\
976	        &\mathbf{u_e^T M_e j} = \mathbf{u_e^T M_{e\sigma} e} \\
977	        &\mathbf{u_f^T M_f h} = \mathbf{u_f^T M_{f \mu} b}
978	
979	    where
980	
981	    * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the discrete curl operator
982	    * :math:`\mathbf{s_m}` and :math:`\mathbf{s_e}` are the integrated magnetic and electric source terms, respectively
983	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_e}` is the edge inner-product matrix
984	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_f}` is the face inner-product matrix
985	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
986	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
987	
988	    By cancelling like-terms and combining the discrete expressions to solve for the magnetic flux density, we obtain:
989	
990	    .. math::
991	        \mathbf{A \, b} = \mathbf{q}
992	
993	    where
994	
995	    * :math:`\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\sigma}^{-1} C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}} + i\omega \mathbf{I}`
996	    * :math:`\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{C M_{e\sigma}^{-1} s_e} - i \omega \mathbf{s_m}`
997	
998	    """
999	
1000	    _solutionType = "bSolution"
1001	    _formulation = "EB"
1002	    fieldsPair = Fields3DMagneticFluxDensity
1003	
1004	    def getA(self, freq):
1005	        r"""System matrix for the frequency provided.
1006	
1007	        This method returns the system matrix for the frequency provided:
1008	
1009	        .. math::
1010	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\sigma}^{-1} C^T M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}} + i\omega \mathbf{I}
1011	
1012	        where
1013	
1014	        * :math:`\mathbf{I}` is the identity matrix
1015	        * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the curl operator
1016	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\sigma}}` is the inner-product matrix for conductivities projected to edges
1017	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\frac{1}{\mu}}}` is the inner-product matrix for inverse permeabilities projected to faces
1018	
1019	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DMagneticFluxDensity`
1020	        for a full description of the formulation.
1021	
1022	        Parameters
1023	        ----------
1024	        freq : float
1025	            The frequency in Hz.
1026

1029	        (n_faces, n_faces) sp.sparse.csr_matrix

1035	        iomega = 1j * omega(freq) * sp.eye(self.mesh.nF)
1036	
1037	        if self.permittivity is None:
1038	            MeSigmaI = self.MeSigmaI
1039	            A = C * (MeSigmaI * (C.T.tocsr() * MfMui)) + iomega

1045

1048	        return A

1348	class Simulation3DCurrentDensity(BaseFDEMSimulation):
1349	    r"""3D FDEM simulation in terms of the current density.
1350	
1351	    This simulation solves for the current density at each frequency.
1352	    In this formulation, the magnetic fields are defined on mesh edges and the
1353	    current densities are defined on mesh faces; i.e. it is an HJ formulation.
1354	    See the *Notes* section for a comprehensive description of the formulation.
1355	
1356	    Parameters
1357	    ----------
1358	    mesh : discretize.base.BaseMesh
1359	        The mesh.
1360	    survey : .frequency_domain.survey.Survey
1361	        The frequency-domain EM survey.
1362	    forward_only : bool, optional
1363	        If ``True``, the factorization for the inverse of the system matrix at each
1364	        frequency is discarded after the fields are computed at that frequency.
1365	        If ``False``, the factorizations of the system matrices for all frequencies are stored.
1366	    permittivity : (n_cells,) numpy.ndarray, optional
1367	        Dielectric permittivity (F/m) defined on the entire mesh. If ``None``, electric displacement
1368	        is ignored. Please note that `permittivity` is not an invertible property, and that future
1369	        development will result in the deprecation of this propery.
1370	    storeJ : bool, optional
1371	        Whether to compute and store the sensitivity matrix.
1372	
1373	    Notes
1374	    -----
1375	    Here, we start with the Maxwell's equations in the frequency-domain where a
1376	    :math:`+i\omega t` Fourier convention is used:
1377	
1378	    .. math::
1379	        \begin{align}
1380	        &\nabla \times \vec{E} + i\omega \vec{B} = - i \omega \vec{S}_m \\
1381	        &\nabla \times \vec{H} - \vec{J} = \vec{S}_e
1382	        \end{align}
1383	
1384	    where :math:`\vec{S}_e` is an electric source term that defines a source current density,
1385	    and :math:`\vec{S}_m` magnetic source term that defines a source magnetic flux density.
1386	    For now, we neglect displacement current (the `permittivity` attribute is ``None``).
1387	    We define the constitutive relations for the electrical resistivity :math:`\rho`
1388	    and magnetic permeability :math:`\mu` as:
1389	
1390	    .. math::
1391	        \vec{E} &= \rho \vec{J} \\
1392	        \vec{B} &= \mu \vec{H}
1393	
1394	    We then take the inner products of all previous expressions with a vector test function :math:`\vec{u}`.
1395	    Through vector calculus identities and the divergence theorem, we obtain:
1396	
1397	    .. math::
1398	        & \int_\Omega (\nabla \times \vec{u}) \cdot \vec{E} \; dv
1399	        - \oint_{\partial \Omega} \vec{u} \cdot (\vec{E} \times \hat{n} ) \, da
1400	        + i \omega \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{B} \, dv
1401	        = - i \omega \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{S}_m dv \\
1402	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot (\nabla \times \vec{H} ) \, dv
1403	        - \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{J} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{S}_j \, dv\\
1404	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{E} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \rho \vec{J} \, dv \\
1405	        & \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \vec{B} \, dv = \int_\Omega \vec{u} \cdot \mu \vec{H} \, dv
1406	
1407	    Assuming natural boundary conditions, the surface integral is zero.
1408	
1409	    The above expressions are discretized in space according to the finite volume method.
1410	    The discrete magnetic fields :math:`\mathbf{h}` are defined on mesh edges,
1411	    and the discrete current densities :math:`\mathbf{j}` are defined on mesh faces.
1412	    This implies :math:`\mathbf{b}` must be defined on mesh edges and :math:`\mathbf{e}` must
1413	    be defined on mesh faces. Where :math:`\mathbf{u_e}` and :math:`\mathbf{u_f}` represent
1414	    test functions discretized to edges and faces, respectively, we obtain the following
1415	    set of discrete inner-products:
1416	
1417	    .. math::
1418	        &\mathbf{u_e^T C^T M_f \, e } + i \omega \mathbf{u_e^T M_e b} = - i\omega \mathbf{u_e^T s_m} \\
1419	        &\mathbf{u_f^T C \, h} - \mathbf{u_f^T j} = \mathbf{u_f^T s_e} \\
1420	        &\mathbf{u_f^T M_f e} = \mathbf{u_f^T M_{f\rho} j} \\
1421	        &\mathbf{u_e^T M_e b} = \mathbf{u_e^T M_{e \mu} h}
1422	
1423	    where
1424	
1425	    * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the discrete curl operator
1426	    * :math:`\mathbf{s_m}` and :math:`\mathbf{s_e}` are the integrated magnetic and electric source terms, respectively
1427	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_e}` is the edge inner-product matrix
1428	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_f}` is the face inner-product matrix
1429	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\rho}}` is the inner-product matrix for resistivities projected to faces
1430	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1431	
1432	    By cancelling like-terms and combining the discrete expressions to solve for the current density, we obtain:
1433	
1434	    .. math::
1435	        \mathbf{A \, j} = \mathbf{q}
1436	
1437	    where
1438	
1439	    * :math:`\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} C^T M_{f\rho} + i\omega \mathbf{I}`
1440	    * :math:`\mathbf{q} = - i \omega \mathbf{s_e} - i \omega \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} s_m}`
1441	
1442	    """
1443	
1444	    _solutionType = "jSolution"
1445	    _formulation = "HJ"
1446	    fieldsPair = Fields3DCurrentDensity
1447	
1448	    permittivity = props.PhysicalProperty("Dielectric permittivity (F/m)")
1449	
1450	    def __init__(
1451	        self, mesh, survey=None, forward_only=False, permittivity=None, **kwargs
1452	    ):
1453	        super().__init__(mesh=mesh, survey=survey, forward_only=forward_only, **kwargs)
1454	        self.permittivity = permittivity
1455	
1456	    def getA(self, freq):
1457	        r"""System matrix for the frequency provided.
1458	
1459	        This method returns the system matrix for the frequency provided.
1460	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
1461	
1462	        .. math::
1463	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} C^T M_{f\rho}} + i\omega \mathbf{I}
1464	
1465	        where
1466	
1467	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\rho}}` is the inner-product matrix for resistivities projected to faces
1468	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1469	
1470	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
1471	        for a full description of the formulation.
1472	
1473	        Parameters
1474	        ----------
1475	        freq : float
1476	            The frequency in Hz.
1477	
1478	        Returns
1479	        -------
1480	        (n_faces, n_faces) sp.sparse.csr_matrix
1481	            The system matrix.
1482	        """
1483	
1484	        MeMuI = self.MeMuI
1485	        MfRho = self.MfRho
1486	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
1487	        iomega = 1j * omega(freq) * sp.eye(self.mesh.nF)
1488	
1489	        if self.permittivity is not None:
1490	            Mfyhati = self._get_face_admittivity_property_matrix(
1491	                freq, invert_model=True
1492	            )
1493	            A = C * MeMuI * C.T.tocsr() * Mfyhati + iomega
1494	        else:
1495	            A = C * MeMuI * C.T.tocsr() * MfRho + iomega
1496	
1497	        if self._makeASymmetric is True:
1498	            return MfRho.T.tocsr() * A
1499	        return A

1501	    def getADeriv_rho(self, freq, u, v, adjoint=False):
1502	        r"""Resistivity derivative operation for the system matrix times a vector.
1503	
1504	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
1505	
1506	        .. math::
1507	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} C^T M_{f\rho}} + i\omega \mathbf{I}
1508	
1509	        where
1510	
1511	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\rho}}` is the inner-product matrix for resistivities projected to faces
1512	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1513	
1514	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
1515	        for a full description of the formulation.
1516	
1517	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\rho}` are the set of model parameters defining the resistivity,
1518	        :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector and :math:`\mathbf{j}` is the discrete current density solution, this method assumes
1519	        the discrete solution is fixed and returns
1520	
1521	        .. math::
1522	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, j})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\sigma}} \, \mathbf{v}
1523	
1524	        Or the adjoint operation
1525	
1526	        .. math::
1527	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, j})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\sigma}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
1528	
1529	        Parameters
1530	        ----------
1531	        freq : float
1532	            The frequency in Hz.
1533	        u : (n_faces,) numpy.ndarray
1534	            The solution for the fields for the current model at the specified frequency.
1535	        v : numpy.ndarray
1536	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_faces,) for the adjoint operation.
1537	        adjoint : bool
1538	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
1539	
1540	        Returns
1541	        -------
1542	        numpy.ndarray
1543	            Derivative of system matrix times a vector. (n_faces,) for the standard operation.
1544	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
1545	        """
1546	
1547	        MeMuI = self.MeMuI
1548	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
1549	
1550	        if adjoint:
1551	            vec = C * (MeMuI.T * (C.T * v))
1552	            return self.MfRhoDeriv(u, vec, adjoint)
1553	        return C * (MeMuI * (C.T * (self.MfRhoDeriv(u, v, adjoint))))

1558	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
1559	
1560	        .. math::
1561	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} C^T M_{f\rho}} + i\omega \mathbf{I}
1562	
1563	        where
1564	
1565	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\rho}}` is the inner-product matrix for resistivities projected to faces
1566	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1567	
1568	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
1569	        for a full description of the formulation.
1570	
1571	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\mu}` are the set of model parameters defining the permeability,
1572	        :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector and :math:`\mathbf{j}` is the discrete current density solution, this method assumes
1573	        the discrete solution is fixed and returns
1574	
1575	        .. math::
1576	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, j})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\mu}} \, \mathbf{v}
1577	
1578	        Or the adjoint operation
1579	
1580	        .. math::
1581	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, j})}{\partial \mathbf{m}_\boldsymbol{\mu}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
1582	
1583	        Parameters
1584	        ----------
1585	        freq : float
1586	            The frequency in Hz.
1587	        u : (n_faces,) numpy.ndarray
1588	            The solution for the fields for the current model at the specified frequency.
1589	        v : numpy.ndarray
1590	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_faces,) for the adjoint operation.
1591	        adjoint : bool
1592	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
1593	
1594	        Returns
1595	        -------
1596	        numpy.ndarray
1597	            Derivative of system matrix times a vector. (n_faces,) for the standard operation.
1598	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
1599	        """
1600	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
1601	        MfRho = self.MfRho
1602	
1603	        MeMuIDeriv = self.MeMuIDeriv(C.T * (MfRho * u))

1611	        # if self._makeASymmetric:

1615	    def getADeriv(self, freq, u, v, adjoint=False):
1616	        r"""Derivative operation for the system matrix times a vector.
1617	
1618	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
1619	
1620	        .. math::
1621	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} C^T M_{f\rho}} + i\omega \mathbf{I}
1622	
1623	        where
1624	
1625	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\rho}}` is the inner-product matrix for resistivities projected to faces
1626	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1627	
1628	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
1629	        for a full description of the formulation.
1630	
1631	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the set of model parameters defining the electromagnetic properties,
1632	        :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector and :math:`\mathbf{j}` is the discrete current density solution, this method assumes
1633	        the discrete solution is fixed and returns
1634	
1635	        .. math::
1636	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, j})}{\partial \mathbf{m}} \, \mathbf{v}
1637	
1638	        Or the adjoint operation
1639	
1640	        .. math::
1641	            \frac{\partial (\mathbf{A \, j})}{\partial \mathbf{m}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
1642	
1643	        Parameters
1644	        ----------
1645	        freq : float
1646	            The frequency in Hz.
1647	        u : (n_faces,) numpy.ndarray
1648	            The solution for the fields for the current model at the specified frequency.
1649	        v : numpy.ndarray
1650	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_faces,) for the adjoint operation.
1651	        adjoint : bool
1652	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
1653	
1654	        Returns
1655	        -------
1656	        numpy.ndarray
1657	            Derivative of system matrix times a vector. (n_faces,) for the standard operation.
1658	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
1659	        """
1660	        if adjoint and self._makeASymmetric:
1661	            v = self.MfRho * v
1662	
1663	        ADeriv = self.getADeriv_rho(freq, u, v, adjoint) + self.getADeriv_mu(
1664	            freq, u, v, adjoint
1665	        )
1666	
1667	        if not adjoint and self._makeASymmetric:
1668	            return self.MfRho.T * ADeriv
1669	
1670	        return ADeriv

1672	    def getRHS(self, freq):
1673	        r"""Right-hand sides for the given frequency.
1674	
1675	        This method returns the right-hand sides for the frequency provided.
1676	        The right-hand side for each source is constructed according to:
1677	
1678	        .. math::
1679	            \mathbf{q} = - i \omega \mathbf{s_e} - i \omega \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} s_m}
1680	
1681	        where
1682	
1683	        * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the discrete curl operator
1684	        * :math:`\mathbf{s_m}` and :math:`\mathbf{s_e}` are the integrated magnetic and electric source terms, respectively
1685	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrices for permeabilities projected to edges
1686	
1687	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
1688	        for a full description of the formulation.
1689	
1690	        Parameters
1691	        ----------
1692	        freq : float
1693	            The frequency in Hz.
1694	
1695	        Returns
1696	        -------
1697	        (n_faces, n_sources) numpy.ndarray
1698	            The right-hand sides.
1699	        """
1700	
1701	        s_m, s_e = self.getSourceTerm(freq)
1702	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
1703	        MeMuI = self.MeMuI
1704	
1705	        RHS = C * (MeMuI * s_m) - 1j * omega(freq) * s_e
1706	        if self._makeASymmetric is True:
1707	            MfRho = self.MfRho
1708	            return MfRho.T * RHS
1709	
1710	        return RHS
1711	
1712	    def getRHSDeriv(self, freq, src, v, adjoint=False):
1713	        r"""Derivative of the right-hand side times a vector for a given source and frequency.
1714	
1715	        The right-hand side for each source is constructed according to:
1716	
1717	        .. math::
1718	            \mathbf{q} = - i \omega \mathbf{s_e} - i \omega \mathbf{C M_{e\mu}^{-1} s_m}
1719	
1720	        where
1721	
1722	        * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the discrete curl operator
1723	        * :math:`\mathbf{s_m}` and :math:`\mathbf{s_e}` are the integrated magnetic and electric source terms, respectively
1724	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrices for permeabilities projected to edges
1725	
1726	        See the *Notes* section of the doc strings for :class:`Simulation3DCurrentDensity`
1727	        for a full description of the formulation.
1728	
1729	        Where :math:`\mathbf{m}` are the set of model parameters and :math:`\mathbf{v}` is a vector,
1730	        this method returns
1731	
1732	        .. math::
1733	            \frac{\partial \mathbf{q_k}}{\partial \mathbf{m}} \, \mathbf{v}
1734	
1735	        Or the adjoint operation
1736	
1737	        .. math::
1738	            \frac{\partial \mathbf{q_k}}{\partial \mathbf{m}}^T \, \mathbf{v}
1739	
1740	        Parameters
1741	        ----------
1742	        freq : int
1743	            The frequency in Hz.
1744	        src : .frequency_domain.sources.BaseFDEMSrc
1745	            The FDEM source object.
1746	        v : numpy.ndarray
1747	            The vector. (n_param,) for the standard operation. (n_faces,) for the adjoint operation.
1748	        adjoint : bool
1749	            Whether to perform the adjoint operation.
1750	
1751	        Returns
1752	        -------
1753	        numpy.ndarray
1754	            Derivative of the right-hand sides times a vector. (n_faces,) for the standard operation.
1755	            (n_param,) for the adjoint operation.
1756	        """
1757	
1758	        # RHS = C * (MeMuI * s_m) - 1j * omega(freq) * s_e
1759	        # if self._makeASymmetric is True:
1760	        #     MfRho = self.MfRho
1761	        #     return MfRho.T*RHS
1762	
1763	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl
1764	        MeMuI = self.MeMuI
1765	        MeMuIDeriv = self.MeMuIDeriv
1766	        s_mDeriv, s_eDeriv = src.evalDeriv(self, adjoint=adjoint)
1767	        s_m, _ = self.getSourceTerm(freq)
1768	
1769	        if adjoint:
1770	            if self._makeASymmetric:
1771	                MfRho = self.MfRho
1772	                v = MfRho * v
1773	            CTv = C.T * v
1774	            return (
1775	                s_mDeriv(MeMuI.T * CTv)
1776	                + MeMuIDeriv(s_m).T * CTv
1777	                - 1j * omega(freq) * s_eDeriv(v)
1778	            )
1779	
1780	        else:
1781	            RHSDeriv = C * (MeMuI * s_mDeriv(v) + MeMuIDeriv(s_m) * v) - 1j * omega(
1782	                freq
1783	            ) * s_eDeriv(v)
1784	
1785	            if self._makeASymmetric:
1786	                MfRho = self.MfRho
1787	                return MfRho.T * RHSDeriv
1788	            return RHSDeriv

1856	    be defined on mesh faces. Where :math:`\mathbf{u_e}` and :math:`\mathbf{u_f}` represent

1858	    set of discrete inner-products:
1859	
1860	    .. math::
1861	        &\mathbf{u_e^T C^T M_f \, e } + i \omega \mathbf{u_e^T M_e b} = - i\omega \mathbf{u_e^T s_m} \\
1862	        &\mathbf{u_f^T C \, h} - \mathbf{u_f^T j} = \mathbf{u_f^T s_e} \\
1863	        &\mathbf{u_f^T M_f e} = \mathbf{u_f^T M_{f\rho} j} \\
1864	        &\mathbf{u_e^T M_e b} = \mathbf{u_e^T M_{e \mu} h}
1865	
1866	    where
1867	
1868	    * :math:`\mathbf{C}` is the discrete curl operator
1869	    * :math:`\mathbf{s_m}` and :math:`\mathbf{s_e}` are the integrated magnetic and electric source terms, respectively
1870	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_e}` is the edge inner-product matrix
1871	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_f}` is the face inner-product matrix
1872	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{f\rho}}` is the inner-product matrix for resistivities projected to faces
1873	    * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1874	
1875	    By cancelling like-terms and combining the discrete expressions to solve for the magnetic field, we obtain:
1876	
1877	    .. math::
1878	        \mathbf{A \, h} = \mathbf{q}
1879	
1880	    where
1881	
1882	    * :math:`\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\rho} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\mu}}`
1883	    * :math:`\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\rho} s_e} - i\omega \mathbf{s_m}`
1884	
1885	    """

1887	    _solutionType = "hSolution"
1888	    _formulation = "HJ"

1892	        r"""System matrix for the frequency provided.
1893	
1894	        This method returns the system matrix for the frequency provided.
1895	        The system matrix at each frequency is given by:
1896	
1897	        .. math::
1898	            \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{C^T M_{f\rho} C} + i\omega \mathbf{M_{e\mu}}
1899	
1900	        where
1901

1903	        * :math:`\mathbf{M_{e\mu}}` is the inner-product matrix for permeabilities projected to edges
1904

1906	        for a full description of the formulation.

1908	        Parameters

1911	            The frequency in Hz.
1912	
1913	        Returns
1914	        -------
1915	        (n_edges, n_edges) sp.sparse.csr_matrix
1916	            The system matrix.

1918	
1919	        MeMu = self.MeMu
1920	        C = self.mesh.edge_curl

319	
320	        \mathbf{C} \mathbf{e} + i \omega \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{s_m} \\
321	        {\mathbf{C}^T \mathbf{M_{\mu^{-1}}^f} \mathbf{b} -
322	        \mathbf{M_{\sigma}^e} \mathbf{e} = \mathbf{s_e}}
323	
324	    We split up the fields and :math:`\mu^{-1}` into primary
325	    (:math:`\mathbf{P}`) and secondary (:math:`\mathbf{S}`) components
326	
327	    - :math:`\mathbf{e} = \mathbf{e^P} + \mathbf{e^S}`
328	    - :math:`\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{b^P} + \mathbf{b^S}`
329	    - :math:`\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\mathbf{-1}} =
330	      \boldsymbol{\mu}^{\mathbf{-1}^\mathbf{P}} +
331	      \boldsymbol{\mu}^{\mathbf{-1}^\mathbf{S}}`
332	
333	    and define a zero-frequency primary simulation, noting that the source is
334	    generated by a divergence free electric current
335	
336	    .. math::
337	
338	        \mathbf{C} \mathbf{e^P} = \mathbf{s_m^P} = 0 \\
339	        {\mathbf{C}^T \mathbf{{M_{\mu^{-1}}^f}^P} \mathbf{b^P} -
340	        \mathbf{M_{\sigma}^e} \mathbf{e^P} = \mathbf{M^e} \mathbf{s_e^P}}
341	
342	    Since :math:`\mathbf{e^P}` is curl-free, divergence-free, we assume that
343	    there is no constant field background, the :math:`\mathbf{e^P} = 0`, so our
344	    primary problem is
345	
346	    .. math::
347	
348	        \mathbf{e^P} =  0 \\
349	            {\mathbf{C}^T \mathbf{{M_{\mu^{-1}}^f}^P} \mathbf{b^P} =
350	            \mathbf{s_e^P}}
351	
352	    Our secondary problem is then
353	
354	    .. math::
355	
356	        \mathbf{C} \mathbf{e^S} + i \omega \mathbf{b^S} =
357	        - i \omega \mathbf{b^P} \\
358	        {\mathbf{C}^T \mathbf{M_{\mu^{-1}}^f} \mathbf{b^S} -
359	        \mathbf{M_{\sigma}^e} \mathbf{e^S} =
360	        -\mathbf{C}^T \mathbf{{M_{\mu^{-1}}^f}^S} \mathbf{b^P}}
361	
362	    Parameters
363	    ----------
364	    receiver_list : list of simpeg.electromagnetics.frequency_domain.receivers.BaseRx
365	        A list of FDEM receivers
366	    frequency : float
367	        Source frequency
368	    location : (dim) numpy.ndarray, default: numpy.r_[0., 0., 0.]
369	        Source location.
370	    moment : float
371	        Magnetic dipole moment amplitude
372	    orientation : {'z', x', 'y'} or (dim) numpy.ndarray
373	        Orientation of the dipole.
374	    mu : float
375	        Background magnetic permeability
376	    """
377	
378	    def __init__(
379	        self,
380	        receiver_list,
381	        frequency,
382	        location=None,
383	        moment=1.0,
384	        orientation="z",

479	    def bPrimary(self, simulation):
480	        """Compute primary magnetic flux density.
481	
482	        Note that we compute analytic vector potential and take numerical
483	        curl do it is divergence free on the mesh.
484	
485	        Parameters
486	        ----------
487	        simulation : BaseFDEMSimulation
488	            A SimPEG FDEM simulation
489	
490	        Returns
491	        -------
492	        numpy.ndarray
493	            Primary magnetic flux density
494	        """
495	        formulation = simulation._formulation
496	        coordinates = "cartesian"
497	
498	        if formulation == "EB":
499	            gridX = simulation.mesh.gridEx
500	            gridY = simulation.mesh.gridEy
501	            gridZ = simulation.mesh.gridEz
502	            C = simulation.mesh.edge_curl
503	
504	        elif formulation == "HJ":
505	            gridX = simulation.mesh.gridFx
506	            gridY = simulation.mesh.gridFy
507	            gridZ = simulation.mesh.gridFz
508	            C = simulation.mesh.edge_curl.T
509	
510	        if simulation.mesh._meshType == "CYL":
511	            coordinates = "cylindrical"
512	
513	            if simulation.mesh.is_symmetric is True:
514	                if not (np.linalg.norm(self.orientation - np.r_[0.0, 0.0, 1.0]) < 1e-6):
515	                    raise AssertionError(
516	                        "for cylindrical symmetry, the dipole must be oriented"
517	                        " in the Z direction"
518	                    )
519	                a = self._srcFct(gridY)[:, 1]
520	
521	                return C * a
522	
523	        ax = self._srcFct(gridX, coordinates)[:, 0]
524	        ay = self._srcFct(gridY, coordinates)[:, 1]
525	        az = self._srcFct(gridZ, coordinates)[:, 2]
526	        a = np.concatenate((ax, ay, az))
527	
528	        return C * a

530	    def hPrimary(self, simulation):
531	        """Compute primary magnetic field.
532	
533	        Note that we compute analytic vector potential and take numerical
534	        curl so that B is divergence-free.
535	
536	        Parameters
537	        ----------
538	        simulation : BaseFDEMSimulation
539	            A SimPEG FDEM simulation
540	
541	        Returns
542	        -------
543	        numpy.ndarray
544	            Primary magnetic field
545	        """
546	        if simulation._formulation == "1D":
547	            if getattr(self, "_1d_h", None) is None:
548	                dipole = self._dipole
549	                out = []
550	                for rx in self.receiver_list:
551	                    if rx.use_source_receiver_offset:
552	                        locs = rx.locations + self.location
553	                    else:
554	                        locs = rx.locations
555	                    h_rx = dipole.magnetic_field(locs)
556	                    out.append(h_rx @ rx.orientation)
557	                self._1d_h = out
558	            return self._1d_h
559	        b = self.bPrimary(simulation)
560	        return 1.0 / self.mu * b
561	
562	    def s_m(self, simulation):
563	        """Magnetic source term (s_m)
564	
565	        Parameters
566	        ----------
567	        simulation : BaseFDEMSimulation
568	            SimPEG FDEM simulation
569	
570	        Returns
571	        -------
572	        numpy.ndarray
573	            Magnetic source term on mesh.
574	        """
575	
576	        b_p = self.bPrimary(simulation)
577	        if simulation._formulation == "HJ":
578	            b_p = simulation.Me * b_p
579	        return -1j * omega(self.frequency) * b_p
580	
581	    def s_e(self, simulation):
582	        """Electric source term (s_e)
583	
584	        Parameters
585	        ----------
586	        simulation : BaseFDEMSimulation
587	            SimPEG FDEM simulation
588	
589	        Returns
590	        -------
591	        numpy.ndarray
592	            Electric source term on mesh.
593	        """
594	
595	        if all(np.r_[self.mu] == np.r_[simulation.mu]):
596	            return Zero()
597	        else:
598	            formulation = simulation._formulation
599	
600	            if formulation == "EB":
601	                mui_s = simulation.mui - 1.0 / self.mu
602	                MMui_s = simulation.mesh.get_face_inner_product(mui_s)
603	                C = simulation.mesh.edge_curl
604	            elif formulation == "HJ":
605	                mu_s = simulation.mu - self.mu
606	                MMui_s = simulation.mesh.get_edge_inner_product(
607	                    mu_s, invert_matrix=True
608	                )
609	                C = simulation.mesh.edge_curl.T
610	
611	            return -C.T * (MMui_s * self.bPrimary(simulation))
612	
613	    def s_eDeriv(self, simulation, v, adjoint=False):
614	        if not hasattr(simulation, "muMap") or not hasattr(simulation, "muiMap"):
615	            return Zero()
616	        else:
617	            formulation = simulation._formulation
618	
619	            if formulation == "EB":
620	                mui_s = simulation.mui - 1.0 / self.mu
621	                MMui_sDeriv = (
622	                    simulation.mesh.get_face_inner_product_deriv(mui_s)(
623	                        self.bPrimary(simulation)
624	                    )
625	                    * simulation.muiDeriv
626	                )
627	                C = simulation.mesh.edge_curl
628	
629	                if adjoint:
630	                    return -MMui_sDeriv.T * (C * v)
631	
632	                return -C.T * (MMui_sDeriv * v)
633	
634	            elif formulation == "HJ":
635	                return Zero()
636	                # raise NotImplementedError
637	                mu_s = simulation.mu - self.mu
638	                MMui_s = simulation.mesh.get_edge_inner_product(
639	                    mu_s, invert_matrix=True
640	                )
641	                C = simulation.mesh.edge_curl.T
642	
643	                return -C.T * (MMui_s * self.bPrimary(simulation))

8	class FieldsFDEM(Fields):
9	    r"""Base class for storing FDEM fields.
10	
11	    FDEM fields classes are used to store the discrete solution of the fields for a
12	    corresponding FDEM simulation; see :class:`.BaseFDEMSimulation`.
13	    Only one field type (e.g. ``'e'``, ``'j'``, ``'h'``, or ``'b'``) is stored, but certain field types
14	    can be rapidly computed and returned on the fly. The field type that is stored and the
15	    field types that can be returned depend on the formulation used by the associated simulation class.
16	    Once a field object has been created, the individual fields can be accessed; see the example below.
17	
18	    Parameters
19	    ----------
20	    simulation : .BaseFDEMSimulation
21	        The FDEM simulation object used to compute the discrete field solution.
22	
23	    Example
24	    -------
25	    We want to access the fields for a discrete solution with :math:`\mathbf{e}` discretized
26	    to edges and :math:`\mathbf{b}` discretized to faces. To extract the fields for all sources:
27	
28	    .. code-block:: python
29	
30	        f = simulation.fields(m)
31	        e = f[:,'e']
32	        b = f[:,'b']
33	
34	    The array ``e`` returned will have shape (`n_edges`, `n_sources`). And the array ``b``
35	    returned will have shape (`n_faces`, `n_sources`). We can also extract the fields for
36	    a subset of the source list used for the simulation as follows:
37	
38	    .. code-block:: python
39	
40	        f = simulation.fields(m)
41	        e = f[source_list,'e']
42	        b = f[source_list,'b']
43	
44	    """
45	
46	    def __init__(self, simulation):
47	        dtype = complex
48	        super().__init__(simulation=simulation, dtype=dtype)
49	
50	    def _GLoc(self, fieldType):
51	        """Return grid locations of the fieldType.
52	
53	        Parameters
54	        ----------
55	        fieldType : str
56	            The field type.
57	
58	        Returns
59	        -------
60	        str
61	            The grid locations. One of {``'CC'``, ``'N'``, ``'E'``, ``'F'``}.
62	        """
63	        return self.aliasFields[fieldType][1]
64	
65	    def _e(self, solution, source_list):
66	        """
67	        Total electric field is sum of primary and secondary
68	
69	        :param numpy.ndarray solution: field we solved for
70	        :param list source_list: list of sources
71	        :rtype: numpy.ndarray
72	        :return: total electric field
73	        """
74	        if (
75	            getattr(self, "_ePrimary", None) is None
76	            or getattr(self, "_eSecondary", None) is None
77	        ):
78	            raise NotImplementedError(
79	                "Getting e from {0!s} is not implemented".format(
80	                    self.knownFields.keys()[0]
81	                )
82	            )
83	
84	        return self._ePrimary(solution, source_list) + self._eSecondary(
85	            solution, source_list
86	        )

88	    def _b(self, solution, source_list):
89	        """
90	        Total magnetic flux density is sum of primary and secondary
91	
92	        :param numpy.ndarray solution: field we solved for
93	        :param list source_list: list of sources
94	        :rtype: numpy.ndarray
95	        :return: total magnetic flux density
